name: multiply by splitting into fewer sub-products
mechanism: split each number into halves (or k parts), compute fewer than the naive number of sub-products by exploiting that the cross terms can be recovered from sums of products of sums, and recombine with shifts and additions, recursing on the sub-products

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Karatsuba algorithm' in section Computational mathematics / Number theoretic algorithms:
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Karatsuba algorithm': an efficient procedure for multiplying large numbers
List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Toom–Cook multiplication': (Toom3) a multiplication algorithm for large integers

fails_when: constant factors make it lose below a size threshold
